answer.rationale:
The strongest signal is temporal: a release landed 2 hours ago and write-path p99 began climbing 90 minutes ago, which fits a release-induced regression better than the alternatives. Peak settlement load is a confound, but load has been peaking daily without this symptom, so the release is the newest variable. Rollback is also the most reversible of the candidates and does not move customer writes across regions or shed them, which matters given the objective of not losing writes.

I want memory_b1 verified because it is the memory doing the most work in this decision and the consolidated summary is thin: it says rollback cleared a 'checkout error spike,' which is an error-rate symptom on a read-ish path, not a climbing write-path latency curve. If the archived record shows a different failure mode, the analogy weakens substantially and I should reconsider. I want memory_b5 verified because it is the best competing action: it claims routing report queries to replicas recovered transactional write latency the same day, which is exactly the symptom I have now. If that record shows the primary was saturated by read load rather than by a code change, replica routing becomes the better single intervention during a write-heavy peak.

Risk I am explicitly flagging: every inherited memory here is a success story with the source archived. That is a survivorship-shaped record — no failed rollbacks, no failovers that dropped in-flight writes, no capacity adds that arrived too late. Treating this set as a balanced prior would overstate how reliably these interventions work. The consolidated summaries have also lost the conditions that made each one work, which is precisely the detail I need to know whether day-74 resembles day-18.

I am therefore not committing to a full rollback. I will roll back on a guarded canary cohort first, using the staged gating capability memory_b6 describes, and watch write-path p99 in that cohort against the rest of the fleet. If latency in the cohort separates within the observation window, the release is confirmed and I widen. If it does not, the load hypothesis gains weight and the next window should go to replica routing (b5) or headroom (b3). Note that a small cohort during peak settlement may not carry enough write volume to resolve the signal quickly; if the cohort readout is ambiguous rather than negative, I should say so rather than read it as exoneration of the release.
